highlightAliases.old: CRT: NYHA II–IV HFREF, EF ≤35%, QRS ≥150 ms; improves symptoms/survival even in octogenarians, unlike ICD (p1184).
highlightAliases.new: CRT: the strongest standard indication includes LVEF ≤35%, sinus rhythm, LBBB and QRS ≥150 ms, with NYHA II, III or ambulatory IV symptoms despite guideline-directed therapy. In selected older adults, CRT improves symptoms, quality of life and survival. ICD therapy targets arrhythmic sudden death (p1184, AHA/ACC/HFSA 2022).

highlightAliases.old: Only SGLT2 inhibitors show consistent benefit in HFPEF trials to date (p1184).
highlightAliases.new: SGLT2 inhibitors reduced HF events in preserved/mildly reduced EF trials. Subsequent FINEARTS-HF also demonstrated a reduction with finerenone in the composite rate of total worsening HF events and cardiovascular deaths among participants with LVEF ≥40% (p1184 describes the earlier evidence).

highlightAliases.old: EMPEROR-Preserved (n=5988, EF >40%): death/HF hospitalization HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.69–0.90, p<0.001), driven by fewer HF hospitalizations; effect consistent regardless of diabetes status (p1188). Dapagliflozin also improved symptoms/exercise function over 12wk in the smaller Preserved-HF trial (n=324) (Table 76-11, p1185).
highlightAliases.new: EMPEROR-Preserved: in 5,988 patients with EF >40%, empagliflozin reduced the combined risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for HF (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.69–0.90, p<0.001), mainly through fewer HF hospitalizations. Results were consistent regardless of diabetes. PRESERVED-HF, a smaller dapagliflozin trial of 324 patients, assessed symptoms and exercise function at 12 weeks (p1185, 1188).

highlightAliases.old: β-blockers: the book says carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, and bisoprolol (the 3 US-approved for HF) are "the only three" proven and "should be used" — but the same page reports SENIORS: nebivolol significantly lowered death/CV hospitalization in patients ≥70 (p1179). Book contradicts itself: pick the 3 for "which β-blockers should be used", but don't reject nebivolol as "no outcome benefit". Metoprolol tartrate is an acceptable titration-phase alternative (p1179).
highlightAliases.new: The three guideline-recommended HFrEF beta blockers are carvedilol, metoprolol succinate and bisoprolol. US labeling for bisoprolol alone is for hypertension, although its HFrEF efficacy is established. Among 2,128 patients aged ≥70, SENIORS found a benefit from nebivolol on the composite of death or cardiovascular hospitalization. These are separate evidence and regulatory questions (p1179).

highlightAliases.old: What creatinine threshold contraindicates mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (spironolactone/eplerenone), and what is spironolactone's typical dose range?
highlightAliases.new: What renal-function and potassium thresholds govern MRA initiation in HFrEF, and which spironolactone dose range does the chapter describe?

highlightAliases.old: Creatinine ≥2.5 mg/dL (or preexisting hyperkalemia); spironolactone 12.5–50 mg once daily (p1181).
highlightAliases.new: For MRA initiation in HFrEF, eGFR must be above 30 mL/min/1.73 m² and potassium below 5.0 mEq/L. Monitor both after starting. The chapter describes spironolactone 12.5–50 mg once daily (p1181, AHA/ACC/HFSA 2022).

highlightAliases.old: EF ≤35% and QRS ≥150 ms in NYHA II–IV HFREF.
highlightAliases.new: The clearest CRT indication is symptomatic NYHA II, III or ambulatory IV HFrEF despite guideline-directed treatment, EF ≤35%, sinus rhythm, LBBB and QRS ≥150 ms.

highlightAliases.old: Unlike an ICD (which reduces sudden death but does not improve quality of life), CRT improves symptoms, exercise tolerance, quality of life, and survival — including in octogenarians (p1184).
highlightAliases.new: CRT can improve function and survival in selected octogenarians. An ICD prevents arrhythmic sudden death (p1184).

highlightAliases.new: Which drug class was tested in EMPEROR-Preserved, and which outcome drove the trial's composite benefit?
Empagliflozin, an SGLT2 inhibitor, reduced cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization in EMPEROR-Preserved (n=5,988, EF >40%, HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.69–0.90).

highlightAliases.new: Fewer HF hospitalizations drove the result, irrespective of diabetes status (p1188).

highlightAliases.old: 500 pg/mL is highly suggestive of active HF; <100 pg/mL makes HF much less likely.
highlightAliases.new: A BNP above 500 pg/mL strongly supports active heart failure in the appropriate clinical context. A BNP below 100 pg/mL makes heart failure much less likely in a nonobese older adult.
